lede: Forex and gold are shut after a punishing week: gold fell about 9% and the S&P 500 8.6% as near-certain December Fed hike bets collided with an AI-led stock rout. Bitcoin hit roughly $55,000 on Saturday, its lowest since September 2024, before climbing back above $60,000.
snapshot_time: Fri 20 Nov close (NY 17:00 ET = 01:00 TRT Sat) · FX/gold closed for the weekend

focus.text: Ended Friday near $3,538 after a $3,503 low, down ~9% on the week and below Monday's 3,571 pivot. Monday's US flash PMIs, then Wednesday's PCE, are the main tests.
Closed near 1.0968 for a third weekly loss as Fed hike pricing kept the dollar near 19-month highs. 1.0953 is the week's low; Monday's euro-area PMIs open the week.

technicals.indicators: Momentum deeply oversold · 14-month low, well below 50- and 200-day MAs · pivot 3,571
technicals.note: Nine straight down sessions have carved lower highs from the early-November peak near 4,149, with Friday closing just above the $3,500 shelf.

technicals.indicators: Capped below the 100-day SMA · three consecutive weekly losses
technicals.note: The pair is pinned under the 1.10 handle, with the former support zone now acting as a ceiling over a narrow 1.0953–1.1035 weekly range.

technicals.indicators: Roughly 20% below the 200-day MA · Fear & Greed 8–12 (extreme fear)
technicals.note: Saturday's flush to about $55,000 was bought back above $60,000, but the daily chart still shows no higher high after the breakdown from the 60–62k floor.
Ether rebounded from about $1,540 but remains in a steep downtrend with momentum at extreme oversold readings.

news.text: US stocks had their worst week in months: S&P 500 −8.6%, Nasdaq about −10%, as an SEC review of Nvidia's accounting deepened the AI sell-off.
Futures price a 25bp hike on 9 Dec at roughly 95% or more; the Fed's pre-meeting blackout starts Saturday 28 Nov.
Kitco's weekly poll: 9 of 15 Wall Street analysts and 46% of retail voters expect further declines after gold's worst week since March.
The US 10-year yield ended the week near 4.94% after haven buying on Friday; the dollar index eased from Thursday's 19-month high.
Brent finished at $92.57, a third straight weekly decline of about 3.4%, despite Friday's small Iran-related bounce.
Bitcoin slid to about $55,000–55,300 early Saturday, its lowest since September 2024, then recovered to around $60,100 by the evening.
More than $2B of leveraged positions were wiped out in 24 hours around Saturday's low, the vast majority of them longs (CoinGlass).
US spot bitcoin ETFs logged about $124M of net outflows on 20 Nov per SoSoValue, extending a week of redemptions above $1.2B.
The Crypto Fear & Greed index sits between 8 and 12, deep in extreme fear; it has stayed at 13 or below since 14 Nov.
Ether bounced about 3.5% to near $1,680 but its 14-day RSI sits near 19, among its most oversold readings of the year.
Ether-treasury firm BTCS told the SEC its $54M Aave loan could face liquidation if prices keep falling (CoinDesk).

weekly_summary.summary: Markets endured a broad liquidation week as hot inflation data and hawkish Fed speakers pushed December hike odds above 90%, while a reported SEC accounting review of Nvidia turned the AI unwind into a rout. The S&P 500 and Dow closed Friday in correction territory and the Nasdaq lost about 10%. Gold suffered its worst week since March, falling about 9% to near $3,538, and the dollar touched a 19-month high before easing. Crypto followed equities lower, with bitcoin breaking $60,000 on Friday and briefly reaching about $55,000 on Saturday.

performance.note: Hike bets, deleveraging; nine straight losses

top_stories.text: An AI-led rout hit Wall Street; Nvidia fell about 14% on Friday on a reported SEC accounting review and chipmakers lost 9–14%.
Governors Cook and others warned against waiting, and markets now price a December hike as near-certain.
Gold slid for nine sessions straight, hitting $3,503 on Friday, its lowest level in over a year.
Bitcoin lost its 60k floor and spot ETFs bled more than $1.2B over the week; the Saturday low near $55,000 was the weakest since September 2024.
BIST 100 dropped 6% on the week to 11,131 and the 10-year Turkish bond yield hit a record near 37%.
